storyboard.addedInformation: Names the price of entry: one thing at a time, no exceptions.
storyboard.claim: Flow has one absolute requirement: uncompromising monotasking.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mihaly pointing firmly at an exhausted office worker: one thing at a time, no split screen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: After the definition of flow (time falls away, ego dissolves): the catch.

storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the authority behind the claim: a lifetime studying chess masters, climbers, surgeons.
storyboard.claim: Split attention blocks flow; Mihaly spent his career studying how people enter it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mihaly speaking directly, no game pieces: the researcher, not any single expert he interviewed.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the rule to the man who proved it.

storyboard.addedInformation: The target makes the abstract condition visible: a single thing to aim at.
storyboard.claim: Flow's first condition: one single clearly defined goal.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A target: a single defined aim, the first condition of flow.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: First of Mihaly's three conditions.

storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the stretch: meaningful work pushed to the limit of ability.
storyboard.claim: The goal must matter deeply, and the task must sit at the edge of ability.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mihaly beside the everyman straining upward toward something just within reach.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Conditions two and three: meaning plus the edge.

storyboard.addedInformation: The spectrum shows the sweet spot between the two failures the narrator names.
storyboard.claim: Too easy means boredom; too hard means anxiety; flow lives exactly between.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A two-pole spectrum: boredom on one end, anxiety on the other, flow in the middle.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The edge made structural: the two ways to miss it.

storyboard.addedInformation: Names the payoff state before the jargon lands.
storyboard.claim: Matching challenge to maximum skill triggers transient hypofrontality.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman thinking hard, fully absorbed: challenge meeting skill.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the map of the edge to what happens inside it.

storyboard.addedInformation: A neuroscientist carries the brain mechanism; the worker shows whose brain it is.
storyboard.claim: The brain's self-doubt, second-guessing and time-tracking regions quiet down.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The neuroscientist explaining while the everyman listens: parts of the prefrontal cortex going dim.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Translates the jargon: which brain parts switch off.

storyboard.addedInformation: The quiet face shows the voice stopping; the audio supplies the quoted questions.
storyboard.claim: The nagging inner critic goes silent as all neural energy routes to the task.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman thinking calmly, untroubled: the second-guessing voice switched off.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The mechanism in first person: the voice you know, silenced.

storyboard.addedInformation: Separates ease from frictionlessness; flags the coming bad news for modern life.
storyboard.claim: Attention turns effortless because self-consciousness is removed, not because it is easy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Mihaly speaking beside an absorbed worker: effort without friction.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sums up the flow state before the modern-lifestyle warning.

storyboard.addedInformation: The slumped phone-clutcher shows the lowest-flow activities the study measured.
storyboard.claim: Tracked across thousands of people, screen scrolling and app-hopping give the least flow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman slumped over a glowing phone: scrolling, TV, app-hopping.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The troubling finding: what modern life actually delivers.

storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the objection: the couch collapse every listener knows.
storyboard.claim: The co-host pushes back: after a 10-hour day you collapse on the couch and reach for the feed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The exhausted worker collapsed, spent: the end of a brutal workday.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the data to the lived objection against it.

storyboard.addedInformation: The phone icon names the device the trance happens on.
storyboard.claim: An hour of Instagram or TikTok feels like a trance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A modern smartphone in hand, the worker staring into it: the scroll-trance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The objection stated: scrolling feels like flow.

storyboard.addedInformation: The startled face shows the lost hour; the quiet critic is the puzzle, not the proof.
storyboard.claim: Time vanishes and the inner critic quiets, so why is this not a relaxing flow?
storyboard.concreteVisual: The worker staring at the phone, startled: five minutes meant, an hour gone.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sharpens the challenge: it mimics flow's two signatures.

storyboard.addedInformation: The struck phrase rejects the label outright; no flow imagery is staged.
storyboard.claim: The answer: this is not flow, it is passive distraction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The analyst correcting, no trance imagery staged plainly: the label is refused.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The verdict on the objection.

storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the psychologists' colder name for the trance.
storyboard.claim: It is numbing out; the difference is how the brain is engaged.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The analyst speaking directly: the mechanics, not the feeling, decide.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the state and points at the machinery beneath it.

storyboard.addedInformation: The compass shows the self-set goal; the climb shows top-down effort.
storyboard.claim: Flow is active top-down engagement: set a goal, push your skills, climb.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The worker climbing purposefully, compass in hand: an active ascent toward a chosen goal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The first half of the mechanics: what flow is.

storyboard.addedInformation: The absorbed thinker shows intensity without self-consciousness.
storyboard.claim: In flow the brain is highly organized and intensely active, just free of ego.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The worker thinking with full focus, face calm: intense work, no inner critic.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Completes the flow picture: busy brain, silent ego.

storyboard.addedInformation: The limp posture shows passivity: the screen acts, he only reacts.
storyboard.claim: Doomscrolling is bottom-up: the brain passively reacts to rapid external stimuli.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The worker slumped, phone glowing up at him: reacting, not choosing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The mirror half: what scrolling is.

storyboard.addedInformation: The reaching hand shows the peck reflex before the pigeon is named.
storyboard.claim: Bright colors, loud noises, outrage triggers: no skill, no goal, only mild dissociation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The worker anxiously reaching for the glowing phone: hooked by flashes and triggers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: What the stimuli are and what they cost: skill and purpose.

storyboard.addedInformation: The emptied posture is the aftereffect the audio describes.
storyboard.claim: Flow leaves you energized; passive scrolling leaves you drained and hollow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The worker slumped and emptied after the scroll: the hollow comedown.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The test that tells them apart: how you feel after.

storyboard.addedInformation: The laboratory box makes the peck-for-pellet image literal against the climber.
storyboard.claim: In flow you are a climber choosing; scrolling you are a pigeon pecking a lever for pellets.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Skinner box with its lever and pellets: the passive pecker, not the active climber.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The episode's image for everything just described.

storyboard.addedInformation: The water shows the river of flow; the second figure shows who pulls you out of it.
storyboard.claim: You cannot flow down the river while an algorithm drags you out by the ankles to sell to you.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The tech ethicist at the puppet strings, the worker hauled up out of the flowing river and dangling, unable to flow, held for sale.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the pigeon to the river it cannot swim: the algorithm's hand.

storyboard.addedInformation: Exhaustion explains the choice: the phone wins because flow takes energy.
storyboard.claim: The tragic irony: we pick passive scrolling because we feel too tired to attempt flow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The depleted worker choosing the phone over effort: too tired to climb.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Why the pigeon wins: exhaustion.

storyboard.addedInformation: The red-lined worker embodies the third structural force: societal exhaustion.
storyboard.claim: The third force eroding focus: a profoundly exhausted society running its engine in the red.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The hollow-eyed worker running on empty: an engine past its limit.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the symptom (choosing the scroll) to the force behind it.

storyboard.addedInformation: The overheated machine never rests: switching and distractions burn it nonstop.
storyboard.claim: We burn unprecedented cognitive energy and never let the machinery cool.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The burned-out worker, head down: a machine denied its cooldown.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: What running in the red burns: the brain's reserves.

storyboard.addedInformation: The physician himself opens the door to the Harvard lab.
storyboard.claim: Enter the Harvard sleep lab with Dr. Charles Czeisler.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The sleep physician gesturing into his sterile observation room.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the theory of exhaustion to the lab that measures it.

storyboard.addedInformation: The sterile room plus the sleepless subject shows the experiment's severity.
storyboard.claim: A sterile, constant room where subjects are kept awake 24, 36, even 48 hours.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The physician indicating his sleepless subject under unblinking lights.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The conditions of the experiment.

storyboard.addedInformation: The game icon shows the child-simple test that still defeats the sleepless.
storyboard.claim: Subjects play the simplest button-press games a child could do.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A simple game: press the button when the shape appears.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The test itself: almost insultingly simple.

storyboard.addedInformation: The physician watches; the subject comes apart: the dismantling made visible.
storyboard.claim: He watches their brains systematically dismantle.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The physician observing his subject coming undone under sleeplessness.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the simple test to the devastating result.

storyboard.addedInformation: The straining face shows memory dissolving in real time.
storyboard.claim: Response times collapse; short-term memories dissolve before his eyes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The sleepless subject straining to hold a thought that slips away.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The dismantling itemized: speed, then memory.

storyboard.addedInformation: Eyes open, brain rebooting: the microsleep the audio describes.
storyboard.claim: Shapes forgotten in 3 seconds; microsleeps reboot the wide-open brain for fractions of a second.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The subject slumped yet staring: awake-eyed, briefly switched off, missing everything.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The failure at its most granular: seconds-long forgetting.

storyboard.addedInformation: The physician's verdict reframes sleep as equipment, not indulgence.
storyboard.claim: Sleep is not luxury or weakness: it is the ultimate attention technology.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The sleep physician stating it plainly: sleep as precision equipment.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the wreckage to what prevents it.

storyboard.addedInformation: The depleted body shows biology, not attitude.
storyboard.claim: It is biological: chronic exhaustion throws the body into permanent physiological emergency.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The exhausted worker's body giving out: a system in emergency.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Why the technology works: the need is physical.

storyboard.addedInformation: The overwhelmed face shows a brain that cannot localize its work.
storyboard.claim: The severely underslept brain cannot maintain localized operations.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The sleepless worker coming apart: a brain unable to hold its stations.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The emergency specified: the brain loses its organization.

storyboard.addedInformation: The analyst delivers the scale; the sleepless worker is one of the 40%.
storyboard.claim: The crisis scale: 40 percent of Americans are chronically sleep deprived.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The analyst stating the figure beside a sleepless worker.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the mechanism to its terrifying scope.

storyboard.addedInformation: The clock shows the stolen minutes; the teenager shows whose nights shrank.
storyboard.claim: Over the past century the average child has lost 85 minutes of sleep a night.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A clock over a sleepless teenager in a dark bedroom: 85 minutes gone nightly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The scope narrowed to children and a century of loss.

storyboard.addedInformation: The bedroom glow shows the tenfold exposure the audio cites.
storyboard.claim: We swim in artificial light: ten times more exposure than fifty years ago.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The worker bathed in harsh artificial glow at night: drowning in light.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The suspected culprit behind the lost sleep.

storyboard.addedInformation: The contrast lands: ancient solar bodies under unnatural light.
storyboard.claim: For millions of years human bodies evolved to the sun's rhythms; that light confuses them.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The worker under an unnatural glow: a solar animal out of its rhythm.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Why the light matters: deep evolutionary wiring.

storyboard.addedInformation: The physician traces the chain: sunset, pineal gland, melatonin, sleep.
storyboard.claim: As sunlight fades the pineal gland releases melatonin, starting the sleep sequence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The physician explaining the natural wind-down: dusk triggering sleep chemistry.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The healthy sequence, before screens break it.

storyboard.addedInformation: The phone names the diode source tricking ancient eyes at 11:30 p.m.
storyboard.claim: Blue-lit screens at night hit the eye's receptors and fool ancient biology into seeing noon.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A smartphone glowing blue in a dark bedroom: midnight light read as midday.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The break in the chain: the screen hijacks the sunset signal.
